stories.headline: How the Knicks celebrated their long-awaited championship in the offseason
stories.summary: From Jalen Brunson's SNL appearance to KAT's wedding, it all began with one event that turned into a domino effect: a Knicks title.
stories.body:
2026 was a season to remember for the New York Knicks, with the iconic franchise winning its first NBA championship in half a century.

As a welcome consequence of the title run, it was also a particularly long season for New York, stretching from October to mid-June. So when the offseason finally arrived, with a championship to celebrate, it was a safe bet the Knicks would make the most of it.

Make the most of it they did. From a euphoric Manhattan parade to "Saturday Night Live," the Knicks had one of the most memorable NBA offseasons in recent memory.

With New York's next regular season starting Tuesday, here's a look back at what the defending champions got up to over the summer.

A long-awaited parade

A unique quirk in New York City history meant that while the Knicks have won three NBA titles, the team had never had a ticker-tape parade. That changed in June, when the 2026 Knicks got their trip down the city's streets.

Unsurprisingly, it was a raucous event. Fans from across the New York metropolitan area flocked to the city well before sunrise to line up for a spot along the route, and attendance reached capacity three hours before the parade's scheduled start. Once the parade did get underway, it was one to remember, featuring a case of mistaken identity for Tyler Kolek, celebrity cameos and chants of "MVP" for the New York City Department of Sanitation.

Karl-Anthony Towns ties the knot

One Knicks star had some particularly important personal business to attend to over the offseason break.

Karl-Anthony Towns, who had proposed on Christmas Day the year prior, said "I do" with his now-wife, Jordyn Woods. The guest list for the star-studded couple's wedding was unsurprisingly packed -- in addition to Towns' New York teammates, Michael B. Jordan and Justin and Hailey Bieber were both reportedly in Malibu for the occasion.

Jalen Brunson hosts SNL
Season 52 of "Saturday Night Live" opened in September with a host familiar to city sports fans (and probably non-sports fans, too, at this point): star point guard Jalen Brunson.

But while Brunson was the host and guest actor in that night's skits, he wasn't alone in representing the team -- Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart were all in the audience for his monologue, with Brunson bantering with his teammates before they eventually joined him on stage at the segment's conclusion.

World Cup appearances

Beyond the NBA Finals, the FIFA World Cup was another event taking the world by storm, and it was part of the Knicks' championship tour.

Accessorized in sunglasses, Hart, Bridges and Anunoby sat in the New York Jets' suite at New York/New Jersey Stadium for France's match against Senegal just days after their win. When the trio appeared on the jumbotron, the stadium roared as Bridges pointed to his "New York" Knicks wordmarked hat. Hart was also on hand for England's win over Norway.

The Knicks ... they went international with it.

A night at the ESPYS

With the ESPYS in New York City months after their championship, it was only right the Knicks took home multiple awards in a handful of categories. Overall, the Knicks won the award for Best Team, while Brunson won three ESPYs for Best Male Athlete, Best NBA Player and Best Championship Performance for his 45-point Game 5 outing.

Anunoby took home the ESPY for Best Play for his final second tip-in at the end of Game 4, which sent Madison Square Garden into a frenzy.

Knicks go Hollywood

Perhaps Brunson wanted more than "Saturday Night Live." The 6-foot-2 guard also put on his acting mask for a special guest appearance on "Law & Order: SVU," which is scheduled to air on Nov. 5. While his role wasn't revealed, cameras caught Brunson on set, police badge and all.

READ MORE: Jalen Brunson to guest star on "Law & Order: SVU"

Brunson isn't the only Knicks player to make a cameo on a crime show. Anunoby will also guest star in Season 4 of the CBS hit show "Elsbeth." His role also wasn't revealed. But between Brunson, Anunoby and Towns' cameo in "The Devil Wears Prada 2" alongside Anne Hathaway, who also stamped her Knicks fandom, we wouldn't be surprised if the Knicks earn a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in the future.

Baseball Knicks

There's nothing like being celebrated by one of the biggest brands in baseball. In June, Brunson and Hart threw out the ceremonial first pitch ahead of the New York Yankees' matchup against the Chicago White Sox -- both at the same time. What a flex, right? Even better: The Yankees won the game 10-5, with 11 strikeouts total.

But that wasn't the end of the Knicks' partnership with the Yankees. In September, the franchise celebrated Hart with a bobblehead night of his own. Hart's figurine wore a white Yankees headband and jersey and carried a basketball, and he also threw out the first pitch for New York's doubleheader against the Baltimore Orioles.

stories.headline: James Maddison apologises to Coventry fans for Tottenham goal celebration
stories.summary: James Maddison has apologised to the Coventry City fans for his goal celebration on Monday night.
stories.body:
James Maddison has apologised to the Coventry City fans for his goal celebration on Monday night.

Maddison opened the scoring for Tottenham Hotspur in their 3-1 win with a beautiful curling effort. It was his first start in 526 days after a serious knee injury and came against his first club from his hometown.

Maddison posted a picture alongside Coventry fans, holding up their shirt, on Tuesday to explain his actions while he celebrated.

"I had already planned my first goal back," he said via social media. "I was kissing the badge of this club who has supported me and my family through the darkest days of my career over the past 18 months.

"I absolutely adore and love Coventry City. All my close friends and family know that.

"I'm a fan and always will be and I will 100% apologise to anyone who thought the timing was bad as my first goal back just happened to be against my hometown club.

"Good luck to Frank [Lampard] and the boys for the rest of the season."

Maddison helped Tottenham claim their first Premier League win of the season, rising them from the foot of the table.

Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies were also on the scoresheet on a night which saw Dejan Kulusevski make his own long-anticipated comeback from a knee injury.

- Dejan Kulusevski explains why he is 'different' after Tottenham injury hell

- Tottenham left to mull cost of win over Coventry despite James Maddison, Dejan Kulusevski returns

- Maddison scores in 'dream' return as Spurs get 1st PL win of season

Maddison had returned from a damaged anterior cruciate ligament in April and had made a series of substitute appearances but started for the first time since against Coventry.

"Even though they've brought in a lot of attacking talent, he will still think no one's better than him because he's that type of character," pundit Jamie Carragher told Sky Sports about Maddison.

"He has that football arrogance that I like in players.

"It will be interesting to see where he fits in eventually because there are a lot of players at Tottenham in the attacking positions, especially with Kulusevski back."

stories.headline: Christian Horner opposed Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull move: 'Shouldn't have been promoted'
stories.summary: Christian Horner has opened up on his reservations about Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull tenure in 2025, claiming the New Zealander "really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."
stories.body:
Christian Horner has opened up on his reservations about Liam Lawson's short-lived Red Bull tenure in 2025, claiming the New Zealander "really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

The inexperienced Lawson was surprisingly picked to replace Sergio Pérez as Max Verstappen's new teammate in December 2024, but former team boss Horner says in his new autobiography, Drive, that he was uneasy with the decision and that it was Red Bull adviser Helmut Marko who pushed for the promotion.

Lawson was dropped after only two races, before Red Bull swiftly turned to Yuki Tsunoda.

"Liam was another racer from the junior programme and Helmut had championed the promotion, but I felt uncomfortable," Horner wrote.

"He was young and inexperienced, with only eleven Formula One races to his name, and we would be asking a huge amount from him."

Horner also accused Marko of playing political games over the decision, claiming the Austrian had told Lawson he was responsible for securing the drive.

"Meanwhile, Helmut was playing games," Horner wrote. "Before the final race of the season in Abu Dhabi, he had informed Liam that he would be driving for Red Bull because of his influence.

"When I challenged Helmut on this, he typically denied everything."

Lawson was promoted following Pérez's difficult 2024 campaign, which saw Red Bull finish third in the constructors' championship despite Verstappen winning his fourth consecutive drivers' title.

The New Zealander had impressed during two spells with the team's junior outfit but struggled immediately after stepping up to Red Bull.

He qualified 18th for the season-opening Australian Grand Prix before crashing out of the race, and then qualified last for both the sprint and the race in China.

"Liam only lasted two races," Horner wrote. "He struggled in pre-season testing and was clearly uncomfortable with the RB21's difficult handling characteristics.

"His confidence was smashed and, as with Pierre Gasly and Alex Albon, his arrival at Red Bull had come too soon.

"Sensing that the pressure on Liam was unfair, we replaced him."

- Horner: Red Bull blocked moves for Leclerc and Alonso

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How he could shake up Ferrari's future

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title at the US Grand Prix

Horner said Honda, Red Bull's engine partner at the time, welcomed the decision to promote Japanese driver Tsunoda.

"The move back [to Racing] Bulls was tough for Liam," Horner wrote. "But he really shouldn't have been promoted in the first place."

Lawson returned to Racing Bulls, while Tsunoda remained alongside Verstappen for the rest of the 2025 season.

Horner was subsequently dismissed as Red Bull team principal and CEO in July 2025.

Lawson said earlier this year that Red Bull created a false narrative around the reasons behind his early exit from the team. The 24-year-old said he wasn't "mentally struggling" and that Red Bull had actually pushed him towards a "wild" setup change to find performance, which ultimately hampered his pace. He added that he now pretends in his mind he "never even went there."

Drive, Christian Horner's autobiography, will be released on Oct. 22.

stories.headline: José Mourinho on Vinícius Jr.: 'No player untouchable at Real Madrid'
stories.summary: José Mourinho insisted that no player is "untouchable" at Real Madrid, as Vinícius Júnior prepares to return to the starting Xl for Wednesday's UCL match.
stories.body:
José Mourinho insisted that no player is "untouchable" at Real Madrid, as Vinícius Júnior prepares to return to the starting Xl for Wednesday's Champions League game with RB Leipzig.

Vinícius is currently serving a four-game ban in LaLiga and so is only available to play in Europe, where he made an underwhelming appearance away at Roma last week, being substituted on 58 minutes as his replacement, Endrick, inspired a 4-3 win.

Mourinho has consistently backed the Brazil international this season, despite a run of poor form which has seen him contribute just one goal for his club in all competitions, and competition for his place from Madrid's record summer signing, Yan Diomande.

"Only the badge is untouchable," Mourinho said in a news conference on Tuesday. "I don't like the concept of 'untouchable' players. What makes players untouchable isn't a captain's armband, or how long they've been at the club, or their status. What makes a player untouchable is performance."

Madrid are trailing leaders Barcelona by six points in LaLiga ahead of Sunday's Clásico at Camp Nou, but they have maximum points in the Champions League so far after two wins out of two against Inter Milan and Roma.

However Mourinho said his team couldn't be considered among the favourites to win this season's competition.

"It's very early," Mourinho said. "Right now Real Madrid don't have the objective of winning the Champions League. We have the objective of qualifying [for the knockout phase]. Then, if we get the points that allow us to qualify, then we get to our second objective, to try to avoid the playoffs, which are two games with tension, and they're games you can avoid."

Mourinho made changes to his team for Sunday's LaLiga game with Sevilla at the Bernabéu, playing Arda Güler in central midfield and giving starts to Diomande and Endrick, and was rewarded with a 4-1 win.

"As I said recently, I'm not a stubborn coach," Mourinho said. "There are coaches who have an idea, and live or die by that idea. I'm not that kind of coach, I'm always open to analyse, to understand things and look for the best for the team."

Defender Ibrahima Konaté said Mourinho has "an aura that not many managers have."

"He doesn't need to speak, and everyone will listen and respect him," Konaté said. "He's a great manager, and everyone here at this club wants success with him."

Konaté was also asked about an incident in September in which he, Kylian Mbappé and Vinicius refused to wear a pre-match T-shirt supporting the Spanish city of Ceuta, in the midst of a migration crisis.

"To be honest, I didn't really understand what was on the shirt," Konaté said on Tuesday. "You have to understand, I'm from France, but my parents came from Africa. Many things happen, and many people are in the same situation as me... In that situation, I didn't understand what it meant on the shirt, and I was focused on the game."

stories.headline: Six players finally getting their time in the spotlight in the WNBA Finals
stories.summary: They might not have been instant stars in the WNBA, but these six players are having a huge impact on the Finals.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Kaila Charles got in position for her most important rebound of the season. Her Golden State Valkyries were clinging to a two-point lead in the closing seconds of Saturday's Game 1 of the WNBA Finals. The Dream had just launched a 3-pointer and Atlanta's Angel Reese, the league's top rebounder the past three years, was waiting for a potential tying putback.

But Charles boxed her out and grabbed the missed shot. That led to two free throws by Golden State teammate Gabby Williams to seal the series opener for the Valkyries. In all, Charles got three defensive rebounds in the final 1 minute, 7 seconds of a close, intense game.

"Kai is all about heart and hustle," Golden State coach Natalie Nakase said. "We've really been leaning on [her] in moments when she comes in. She changes the game."

Charles is one of several players making an impact in the Finals who might not have been instant stars when they arrived in the league but have found the right fit.

Others, such as Atlanta's Jordin Canada, have been successful in the past but have now fully stepped into the spotlight this postseason. In Monday's Game 2, Canada registered 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds to help the Dream even the series 1-1 with a 79-65 victory.

Here are six players having breakout moments who have shown that timing is everything.

Gabby Williams: 'Just go at me'

Williams maintains it's less about her blossoming and more about her not being given respect in the past. But statistically, her impact has never been bigger than right now, and her popularity is at its zenith with Valkyries fans. With Williams in her eighth WNBA season but her first in the Bay Area, Golden State has been the best fit for her in every aspect.

The Chicago Sky drafted Williams out of UConn with the No. 4 pick in 2018, and she played there three seasons. She was traded to the Los Angeles Sparks prior to the 2021 campaign, but she didn't play in the WNBA that year as she concentrated on competing in the Olympics with the French national team. Williams' time with Team France has helped expand her game and perhaps even more importantly has made her feel appreciated.

The Sparks traded Williams to the Storm before the 2022 season, and she was with Seattle through 2025, although she played just 10 games in 2023 and 12 in 2024. Then last season, she broke out with the Storm: Williams played all 44 games, made her first All-Star Game, was on the All-Defensive first team and averaged career highs in points, assists and steals.

After signing with Golden State this season, Williams improved her scoring average to a career-best 14.4 points and was again selected to the All-Defensive first team. Making her first appearance in the WNBA Finals, she led the Valkyries with 26 points in Game 1.

"Her 'killer' mode goes up a level every game," Nakase said. "The best thing she told me is, 'Just go at me. Like in games, I need directness.'

"Those are the best players to coach, because you can just say [something] right away and it doesn't waste time. The fact that she told me her coaching style right away made us grow closer together."

Jordin Canada: 'The most rewarding year'

Canada hasn't had to worry about having a WNBA job; she has started more than 70% of her games across a nine-year career. But she has never shined so brightly as she has in 2026, a culmination of her growth and resilience through injuries.

"She's just everything you'd want from a point guard," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said.

Drafted No. 5 out of UCLA in 2018 by Seattle, she won two WNBA titles as a backup to Hall of Famer Sue Bird during four campaigns there.

"I'm a lot older now. I've learned a lot," Canada said of this Finals appearance. "Obviously, I'm in a different role than I was my first two championships of coming off the bench and trying to figure out where I can get in."

After two years with the Los Angeles Sparks, Canada was traded to Atlanta before the 2024 season. Injuries limited her to 20 games in 2024 and 28 in 2025. But she has played all but one game this year while averaging 31.1 minutes, during which she averaged 11.6 points and a career-best 7.3 assists in the regular season with those numbers increasing to 16.7 and 8.7 in the playoffs.

"My leadership has grown over the years, being able to talk more, communicate more, bring my championship experience to this team," Canada said. "Those are just some of the ways that I feel that I have grown. It's been the most rewarding year that I've had."

Veronica Burton: The 'smartest worker'

A three-time Big Ten defensive player of the year at Northwestern, Burton was the No. 7 pick in the 2022 draft and stayed with the Dallas Wings for two seasons. Cut just before the 2024 campaign, Burton was signed by the Connecticut Sun. But she was left available in the expansion draft, and Golden State took her. It has been the perfect fit.

"It's about understanding that when one door closes, that doesn't mean all of them are closed," Burton said of her WNBA path. "It may not go exactly as you initially imagined, but I hope people can learn from my journey."

Burton was the WNBA's Most Improved Player in 2025 and was on the All-Defensive Team this season and last. This year, she averaged a career-high 12.2 points in the regular season and ranked No. 9 in the WNBA in assists (5.7). While her averages have dropped in the playoffs, her impact has endured.

Nakase said that helping Burton reach her best these past two seasons is the same process she has used with other players.

"It's just asking them the questions ... what is your learning style and what do you need from me?" Nakase said. "She said, 'I just need someone to believe in me as a coach.'

"Her work ethic is the best. Last year, she showed up too much, like 8 in the morning. She learned to trust me that you don't always have to be the 'hardest' worker, you have to be the smartest worker."

Kiah Stokes: 'Clicked immediately'

The 6-foot-3 center has as much championship experience as anyone in this series, with three NCAA titles at UConn and three WNBA titles with the Las Vegas Aces. The No. 11 pick in the 2015 draft by the Liberty, Stokes spent five full seasons with New York. (She sat out in 2019.) Then in 2021, she was waived by the Liberty in late June after playing nine games.

Two days later, Las Vegas signed her -- and the best part of her pro career began. She won the 2022, 2023 and 2025 championships with the Aces. Stokes was a valuable part of the team but understandably was overshadowed by perennial league MVP A'ja Wilson.

Now with the Valkyries, Stokes is a full-time starter, averaging her most minutes (22.3) during the regular season since 2020 with New York. Her scoring (3.6) and rebounding (5.8) averages don't stand out, but the way she does everything the Valkyries need -- screening, passing, help defense, rim protection -- has in many ways made this her signature season.

Despite the Game 2 loss, Stokes on Monday joined Brittney Griner (2014) as the only players in WNBA history to record four-plus blocks in consecutive Finals games.

Her personality meshes with that of Nakase, who was an Aces assistant while Stokes was with Las Vegas.

"We clicked immediately," Stokes said. "We understand each other. She understands the game. She understands the work ethic."

Naz Hillmon: 'A reality check'

Hillmon was the program changer at Michigan, the most important recruit in coach Kim Barnes Arico's mission to make the Wolverines a contender. Hillmon led Michigan to its first Sweet 16 in 2021 and its first Elite Eight in 2022, after which she was a second-round pick by the Dream at No. 15. That was a steal for Atlanta: No player in that draft class has played more WNBA regular-season games (201) than Hillmon.

She was an elite scorer at 18.3 points per game over her college career. In the WNBA, she went to Atlanta along with the No. 1 pick in the same draft in Rhyne Howard, who has been one of the Dream's top scorers. Hillmon realized she needed to become a different type of player to excel in the WNBA. She focused more on defense, screening and facilitating. Then she dramatically improved her shooting range, going from just one made 3-pointer across her first three WNBA seasons to 53 in 2025 and 52 in 2026.

"It takes looking in the mirror and seeing that everybody can't be a star player once you get to this level," Hillmon said. "It's a reality check, but I feel I've always been someone who is selfless in doing whatever my team needs me to do. Being an undersized post player, how do I stay in this league as long as I possibly can?"

Hillmon was the WNBA's Sixth Player of the Year last season. She has started all but three of the Dream's games this year, averaging a career-best 9.1 points.

"She has really developed her game the last two years," Smesko said. "She's always been a good cutter and offensive rebounder and somebody who's willing to screen and get other people open. She has really found her rhythm and is also taking on the top defensive assignments."

Kaila Charles: 'Staying the course'

Charles started all 135 games she played at Maryland and was a three-time All-Big Ten first-team selection. But as a 6-foot-1 guard who made just 10 3-pointers in her college career, she fell to the next-to-last pick in the second round, No. 23, of the 2020 draft. However, only four of the 22 players taken ahead of her have played more than Charles' 135 WNBA regular-season games. Many are out of the league, but Charles persevered.

After her first two seasons with Connecticut and brief stints in Atlanta (one game in 2022) and Seattle (four games in 2023), she didn't play in the WNBA in 2024. In 2025, she joined Dallas but was released after 17 games.

Then Golden State called. She had three consecutive seven-day contracts before signing on for the rest of the 2025 campaign. She's now finishing the first season of a two-year deal with the Valkyries.

"I have been cut from multiple different teams, but one thing that never wavered was my belief that I belong," Charles said. "It was just finding a coach that believed in me, finding the right fit, and then just staying the course. I was playing overseas; I was playing here. I was staying ready for my moment."

Nakase praises the resilience of Charles, who represents a blue-collar determination Valkyries fans admire.

"The other day, I was at Safeway [grocery store], and someone gave me some flowers, a random lady," Charles said. "It was just really sweet. I really do feel the love and appreciation."

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previewing Bruins-Stars, all 10 other matchups on Tuesday
stories.summary: Twenty-two teams will be in action this evening. Here's what you need to know.
stories.body:
October is arguably the best month of the year for sports fans, and the NHL is doing its part Tuesday to create another special evening.

No, it's not the 16-game slate of the Frozen Frenzy, but there are 11 games on the calendar, including a number of tantalizing matchups between interconference contenders.

Here's a look at what you need to know for each contest, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

San Jose Sharks at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -205, O/U: 6.5

After a visit to the Maple Leafs on Monday, Macklin Celebrini & Co. head to la Belle Province for a showdown against an as yet underperforming Canadiens team. Celebrini has had quite a bit of success against the Habs, with four goals and five assists in four games against Montreal in his career -- seven of those nine points came in the two matchups in 2025-26.

Colorado Avalanche at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | COL -115, O/U: 6.5

The Avalanche and Devils have faced off 102 times in the regular season in their history -- and once in a Stanley Cup Final that was historic for its intensity as well as Ray Bourque finally winning a title.

Back to current events, any game against a top team like this is a good barometer for a Devils club that is still figuring out what this season is going to look like. And on the other side, whichever member of the Lumber Yard is in the crease, it'll be familiar territory as both are ex-Devils.

Anaheim Ducks at New York Islanders

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -166, O/U: 6.5

Just 24 hours after facing off against the Rangers at Madison Square Garden, the Ducks will take to the ice at UBS Arena on Long Island before a date with the Devils on Thursday and finishing out their trip in Philadelphia on Saturday.

Specific to this game, it's a showdown between two of the top rookies from last season: Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer, who unanimously won the Calder Trophy, and Ducks winger Beckett Sennecke, who finished a point ahead of him in the rookie scoring race.

Los Angeles Kings at Washington Capitals

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WSH -166, O/U: 5.5

The Kings -- a playoff team last season -- are still on the hunt for their first win of the season. Will it be Tuesday? Of note, L.A. lost both games against the Capitals last season (2-1 on Nov. 17 and 3-1 on Dec. 2).

Washington brings a two-game winning streak into this matchup. The Caps are getting contributions from all over, but two offseason additions are leading the goal-scoring charge: Alex Tuch (five goals) and Boone Jenner (four).

Toronto Maple Leafs at Columbus Blue Jackets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CBJ -162, O/U: 6.5

These teams made major news on the eve of opening night when they consummated a trade sending Kirill Marchenko to Toronto and Matthew Knies to Columbus (among six players moved in the swap).

Thus far, Marchenko has been the more lucrative player on the score sheet with nine points in nine games compared to four in seven for Knies. How do they each respond in this game -- and how do the Columbus fans welcome back Marchenko, who signaled an unwillingness to re-sign with the Blue Jackets, which led to the trade?

Winnipeg Jets at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | STL -142, O/U: 5.5

Any game between Central Division foes is a must-watch, but the added wrinkle in any Jets game this fall is the Connor Hellebuyck saga. The latest, per ESPN's Emily Kaplan, is that there are three teams in the mix to trade for the former Hart and Vezina Trophy winner.

Though all of the off-ice business was generating buzz on message boards, the Jets are off to a 4-2-2 start, three points ahead of the Blues heading into this showdown. A key for the Blues? Scoring more than two goals. They've lost all four games in which they've scored two or fewer, and won three of the four in which they've scored more than two goals.

Boston Bruins at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN) | DAL -170, O/U: 5.5

And speaking of U.S. Olympic goaltenders, this contest could feature a showdown between Boston's Jeremy Swayman and Dallas' Jake Oettinger. According to ESPN Research, Oettinger (187) and Swayman (138) and second and third, respectively, for the most wins by an American goalie since 2020-21 (behind Hellebuyck's 197).

On the goal-scoring side, there will be superstars on both sides as David Pastrnak (No. 8), Mikko Rantanen (15) and Jason Robertson (20) all landed in the top 20 of ESPN's annual player rankings.

Minnesota Wild at Edmonton Oilers

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | EDM -130, O/U: 6.5

This matchup has even more star power, with Connor McDavid (No. 1), Leon Draisaitl (6), Quinn Hughes (9) and Kirill Kaprizov (10) all in the top 10. stories.headline: Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili joins rare list of trilogy bouts at UFC 333
stories.summary: ESPN categorizes all 19 of the UFC's trilogies ahead of Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili 3 at UFC 333 on Saturday.
stories.body:
When men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan and former champion Merab Dvalishvili fight in the UFC 333 co-main event on Saturday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, it will be their third meeting, completing the promotion's 20th trilogy.

This weekend's headliners, featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski and undefeated challenger Movsar Evloev, will square off for the first time, but Volkanovski has already been part of a UFC trilogy. His threepeat with Max Holloway several years ago played out far differently from what will unfold in the UFC 333 co-main. That's guaranteed. (Read on to find out why.)

How fitting is it that Saturday's event is numbered 333, a coincidental acknowledgment that when the UFC deals out three of a kind, the fans end up with a winning hand. Usually.

Trilogies come in all shapes with all sizes. Many of the sport's biggest stars have been in one or more, yet at least one UFC three-fight series featured competitors newer fans probably haven't heard of. Some trilogies have had championship-level stakes in each fight, while others have been driven by nothing but a scornful rivalry that makes the fights feel no less consequential. A few trilogies have been one-sided and a couple have concluded without establishing who's better. We did the math.

Other MMA organizations have staged trilogies, and some have played out across multiple promotions, but this list sticks to the 19 all-UFC trilogies to date and sorts them by similarities and distinguishing factors.

Passing the torch
Trilogies in which the winner of the first fight was at the top of the sport, and by the third meeting the opponent was MMA's top fighter

Chuck Liddell vs. Randy Couture
Results:

UFC 43, June 6, 2003: Couture def. Liddell (TKO3) for interim light heavyweight title
UFC 52, April 16, 2005: Liddell def. Couture (KO1) for light heavyweight title
UFC 57, Feb. 4, 2006: Liddell def. Couture (KO2) for light heavyweight title

Notable: In the lead-up to their second meeting, Liddell and Couture coached against each other on the inaugural season of "The Ultimate Fighter," the reality show UFC CEO Dana White often credits with keeping the UFC in business. Through their TV appearances and contrasting fighting styles and personalities, Liddell and Couture helped catapult MMA toward the sports mainstream. Couture is one of just three fighters (along with Tito Ortiz and Matt Hughes) to compete in two UFC trilogies -- this one and a trio of fights with Vitor Belfort.

Georges St-Pierre vs. Matt Hughes
Results:

UFC 50, Oct. 22, 2004: Hughes def. St-Pierre (Sub1) for welterweight title
UFC 65, Nov. 18, 2006: St-Pierre def. Hughes (TKO2) for welterweight title
UFC 79, Dec. 29, 2007: St-Pierre def. Hughes (Sub2) for interim welterweight title

Notable: This is the only UFC trilogy to feature multiple submission finishes. Hughes won by armbar at UFC 50, and St-Pierre ended the trilogy at UFC 79 by submitting Hughes, also by armbar. When the fighters were standing, though, GSP dominated. In their second meeting, he outstruck Hughes 49-10 with two knockdowns. In the third fight, it was 97-10.

A stunning start ... and finish
Trilogies that began with a shocking KO upset, followed by the KO victim scoring two dominant wins

Cain Velasquez vs. Junior Dos Santos
Results:

UFC on Fox, Nov. 12, 2011: Dos Santos def. Velasquez (KO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 155, Dec. 29, 2012: Velasquez def. Dos Santos (UD) for heavyweight title
UFC 166, Oct. 19, 2013: Velasquez def. Dos Santos (TKO5) for heavyweight title

Notable: The first fight lasted barely a minute, as Dos Santos essentially won by one-punch knockout. The rematch and trilogy fight dramatically swung the other way. Velasquez battered JDS for the full 25 minutes of their second meeting, as reflected by one judge awarding him two 10-8 rounds. Velasquez became the first UFC fighter to reach triple-figure significant strikes (111) and double-figure takedowns (11) in a single fight.

Stipe Miocic vs. Daniel Cormier
Results:

UFC 226, July 7, 2018: Cormier def. Miocic (KO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 241, Aug. 17, 2019: Miocic def. Cormier (TKO4) for heavyweight title
UFC 252, Aug. 15, 2020: Miocic def. Cormier (UD) for heavyweight title

Notable: Cormier was light heavyweight champion when he first faced Miocic, and by crushing the heavyweight king with an uppercut, Cormier became the second UFC champ to reign in two weight classes simultaneously. Miocic bounced back in the next two fights, and his victory in the third meeting tied him with Couture for the most UFC heavyweight title-fight wins, with six.

Back and forth (and back)
Trilogies in which the winner of the first fight lost the second, then won the third -- a rarity

Randy Couture vs. Vitor Belfort
Results:

UFC 15, Oct. 17, 1997: Couture def. Belfort (TKO1)
UFC 46, Jan. 31, 2004: Belfort def. Couture (TKO1) for light heavyweight title
UFC 49, Aug. 21, 2004: Couture def. Belfort (TKO3) for light heavyweight title

Notable: Entering the first fight, Belfort was 20 years old and 4-0 as a pro -- all knockouts of a minute, 17 seconds or faster. But Couture, 34, stopped his momentum cold. When they met again six years later, Belfort won in 49 seconds after his glove scraped Couture's eye, causing a corneal abrasion that prompted the cageside doctor to stop the fight. In the third fight, Couture brutalized Belfort for three rounds before that event's doctor had seen enough. This is the only UFC trilogy in which two fights ended by doctor's stoppage.

BJ Penn vs. Matt Hughes
Results:

UFC 46, Jan. 31, 2004: Penn def. Hughes (Sub1) for welterweight title
UFC 63, Sept. 23, 2006: Hughes def. Penn (TKO3) for welterweight title
UFC 123, Nov. 20, 2010: Penn def. Hughes (KO1)

Notable: After two unsuccessful bids for the lightweight championship, Penn moved up to welterweight and won the belt in a stunning upset, ending Hughes' two-year reign and 13-fight winning streak. After Hughes won the rematch to even the score, Penn completed the trilogy in style, knocking out Hughes in 21 seconds -- the fastest finish in a UFC trilogy.

You're just flexing now
Trilogies that ended in a 3-0 sweep

Tito Ortiz vs. Ken Shamrock
Results:

UFC 40, Nov. 12, 2002: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO3) for light heavyweight title
UFC 61, July 8, 2006: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO1)
UFC Ortiz vs. Shamrock 3, Oct. 10, 2006: Ortiz def. Shamrock (TKO1)

Notable: This trilogy is unmatched in its bitter animosity, for sure, and maybe even in one-sidedness. The feud grew out of the brash Ortiz defeating fighters from Shamrock's highly regarded Lion's Den gym, then mocking that team with vulgar gestures and custom T-shirts. Ortiz and Shamrock finally met at UFC 40 amid much anticipation, and the heated buildup drove a pay-per-view buy rate double what the UFC had ever seen.

Frankie Edgar vs. BJ Penn
Results:

UFC 112, April 10, 2010: Edgar def. Penn (UD) for lightweight title
UFC 118, Aug. 28, 2010: Edgar def. Penn (UD) for lightweight title
The Ultimate Fighter 19 Finale, July 6, 2014: Edgar def. Penn (TKO3)

Notable: Penn, who had not lost a lightweight bout in eight years, was a near 8-1 betting favorite in the first fight. Even after Edgar pulled off a narrow upset, he was still the underdog entering the rematch. He won that one more clearly with three 50-45 scorecards, then completed the trilogy with a knockout. Of the UFC's 19 trilogies, 11 have ended with a finish in the third fight. But only two -- both involving Edgar -- ended with a finish after two consecutive decisions. The other was Edgar's series with Gray Maynard.

Alexander Volkanovski vs. Max Holloway
Results:

UFC 245, Dec. 14, 2019: Volkanovski def. Holloway (UD) for featherweight title
UFC 251, July 11, 2020: Volkanovski def. Holloway (SD) for featherweight title
UFC 276, July 2, 2022: Volkanovski def. Holloway (UD) for featherweight title

Notable: Just because this trilogy ended 3-0 doesn't mean Volkanovski had it easy. In the second fight, Holloway knocked him down in each of the first two rounds, forcing the champ to play catch-up. Holloway made Volkanovski work the full five rounds in all three fights. At 75 minutes of total cage time, this is the UFC's longest trilogy.

Let's call it even
Trilogies that ended at 1-1, plus a draw

Frankie Edgar vs. Gray Maynard
Results:

UFC Fight Night, April 2, 2008: Maynard def. Edgar (UD)
UFC 125, Jan. 1, 2011: Maynard vs. Edgar for lightweight title ends in split draw
UFC 136, Oct. 8, 2011: Edgar def. Maynard (KO4) for lightweight title

Notable: The second meeting produced the greatest comeback and the most memorable draw in UFC history. Maynard knocked Edgar down three times in Round 1 while piling up a 47-10 edge in strikes landed. All three judges scored it 10-8, and Edgar was so rocked that he doesn't remember anything from the rounds that followed. He "missed" a great fight. The final meeting also began badly for Edgar, but this time his comeback built toward a late knockout that emphatically evened the score.

Valentina Shevchenko vs. Alexa Grasso
Results:

UFC 285, March 4, 2023: Grasso def. Shevchenko (Sub4) for women's flyweight title
Noche UFC, Sept. 16, 2023: Shevchenko vs. Grasso for women's flyweight title ends in split draw
UFC 306, Sept. 14, 2024: Shevchenko def. Grasso (UD) for women's flyweight title

Notable: The only women's trilogy in UFC history opened with a staggering upset, as Grasso capitalized on an ill-advised spinning attack by Shevchenko to seize control and quickly lock in a choke that ended the champ's six-year unbeaten run. Grasso narrowly held on to the title in a tightly contested second fight. Shevchenko dominated the third meeting, thanks to a change in strategy. Her grappling-heavy approach produced at least one takedown in each of the five rounds, 16 minutes of ground control and a trio of 50-45 scorecards.

Remember me?
Trilogies with at least seven years between fights

Dustin Poirier vs. Max Holloway
Results:

UFC 143, Feb. 4, 2012: Poirier def. Holloway (Sub1) for interim lightweight title
UFC 236, April 13, 2019: Poirier def. Holloway (UD)
UFC 318, July 19, 2025: Holloway def. Poirier (UD) for BMF title

Notable: The first fight was Holloway's UFC debut at 20 years old, and their final meeting 13 years later was Poirier's retirement fight. By winning that third bout, Holloway became the first fighter to win a UFC trilogy after losing the first two matchups.

Leon Edwards vs. Kamaru Usman
Results:

UFC on Fox, Dec. 19, 2015: Usman def. Edwards (UD)
UFC 278, Aug. 20, 2022: Edwards def. Usman (KO5) for welterweight title
UFC 268, March 18, 2023: Edwards def. Usman (MD) for welterweight title

Notable: Usman was 58 seconds from going up 2-0 in this series when an Edwards head kick out of nowhere changed everything. Usman had won 15 fights in a row and was on the verge of tying Anderson Silva's record for the longest UFC win streak at the time. Since that shocking defeat, he's gone 1-3, including another loss to Edwards.

No gold, just (a little) glory
Trilogies in which no championships were on the line

Sam Stout vs. Spencer Fisher
Results:

UFC 58, March 4, 2006: Stout def. Fisher (SD)
UFC Fight Night, June 12, 2007: Fisher def. Stout (UD)
UFC on FX, June 22, 2012: Stout def. Fisher (UD)

Notable: The first meeting was Stout's UFC debut, and apparently both fighters were just warming up. The rematch and trilogy fight each earned fight of the night bonuses. The third meeting had an added emotional element for Stout, as it was his first fight after the death of his coach and brother-in-law, Shawn Tompkins.

Forrest Griffin vs. Tito Ortiz
Results:

UFC 59, April 15, 2006: Ortiz def. Griffin (SD)
UFC 106, Nov. 21, 2009: Griffin def. Ortiz (SD)
UFC 148, July 7, 2012: Griffin def. Ortiz (UD)

Notable: Both competitors were 205-pound champions, just not during any of their three meetings. All three fights happened after Ortiz's title reign from 2000 to 2003. The first fight was before Griffin became champ in 2008, and the other two were after he lost the belt later that same year. The trilogy fight was Griffin's career finale and Ortiz's final UFC appearance.

Charles Oliveira vs. Nik Lentz
Results:

UFC on Versus, June 26, 2011: Oliveira vs. Lentz ends in no contest
UFC Fight Night, May 30, 2015: Oliveira def. Lentz (Sub3)
UFC Fight Night, May 18, 2019: Oliveira def. Lentz (TKO2)

Notable: The first bout appeared to end with an Oliveira rear-naked choke in Round 2, but the Pennsylvania State Athletic Commission ruled that Oliveira had landed an illegal knee and overturned the result to a no-contest. The bout earned both men fight of the night bonuses, as did the second fight.

Dustin Poirier vs. Conor McGregor
Results:

UFC 178, Sept. 27, 2014: McGregor def. Poirier (TKO1)
UFC 257, Jan. 23, 2021: Poirier def. McGregor (TKO2)
UFC 264, July 10, 2021: Poirier def. McGregor (TKO1)

Notable: This rivalry could have fit in the "Remember me?" category because of the seven-year gap between the first and second bouts. But what truly makes this trilogy stand apart from all others is McGregor's star power. He headlined the seven highest-selling pay-per-views in UFC history, and only his bouts with Khabib Nurmagomedov and Nate Diaz outsold his two meetings with Poirier in 2021. McGregor suffered the first two knockout losses of his MMA career in those bouts, the second finish coming by doctor's stoppage after he broke his left tibia and fibula.

Three is not enough?
The only UFC tetralogy -- plus 75% of another

Brandon Moreno vs. Deiveson Figueiredo
Results:

UFC 256, Dec. 12, 2020: Moreno vs. Figueiredo for men's flyweight title ends in majority draw
UFC 263, June 12, 2021: Moreno def. Figueiredo (Sub3) for men's flyweight title
UFC 270, Jan. 22, 2022: Figueiredo def. Moreno (UD) for men's flyweight title
UFC 283, Jan. 21, 2023: Moreno def. Figueiredo (TKO3) for men's flyweight title

Notable: These two flyweights squeezed in four fights over 25 months, faster than many two-fight series. Moreno and Figueiredo each produced heart-pounding moments throughout the four fights, and together they landed exactly 700 strikes. The second fight represented a memorable accomplishment for Moreno when he became the first Mexico-born UFC champion.

Tim Sylvia vs. Andrei Arlovski
Results:

UFC 51, Feb. 5, 2005: Arlovski def. Sylvia (Sub1) for interim heavyweight title
UFC 59, April 15, 2006: Sylvia def. Arlovski (TKO1) for heavyweight title
UFC 61, July 8, 2006: Sylvia def. Arlovski (UD) for heavyweight title
One FC 5, Aug. 31, 2012: Sylvia vs. Arlovski ends no contest in One Championship

Notable: The first fight lasted 47 seconds, with Arlovski's quick knockdown leading to a leg-lock finish. Arlovski nearly repeated the feat in the rematch, dropping Sylvia halfway through Round 1. But after a wobbly Sylvia got back to his feet and Arlovski moved in for a finish, Sylvia caught him with a short uppercut to even the score. Their final UFC meeting turned into a tactical, tentative sparring session, as one might expect from a matchup where each fighter had already felt the other's power. Also as expected, the ornery crowd was unimpressed.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: LeBron James' most notable Madison Square Garden appearances
stories.summary: Here are some of LeBron James' memorable performances at the world's most famous arena throughout the years as he faces the Knicks on Tuesday.
stories.body:
LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers will travel to Madison Square Garden to face the New York Knicks on Tuesday in the season opener for both teams, which will also be James' debut with the Sixers.

James has played 34 games in the "World's Most Famous Arena," amassing a 24-10 record while averaging 28.1 points, 7.4 assists and 6.9 rebounds per game.

He has met the Knicks only once in the postseason: the first round of the 2012 playoffs, which the Miami Heat won 4-1. He averaged 27.8 points, 6.2 rebounds and 5.6 assists, and scored less than 20 points only once in that series.

James has had his share of memorable games at Madison Square Garden throughout the years. Here's a look at some of the most notable.

Feb. 1, 2026: 22 points, 6 assists, 5 rebounds, 60% shooting

Game result: 112-100, Lakers loss

James had respectable numbers in his most recent trip to Madison Square Garden, shooting 60% from the field, and the Lakers were up on the Knicks heading into halftime. New York came roaring back, however, scoring 38 points to the Lakers' 26 in the third quarter and hanging on for a 12-point victory.

Earlier that day, James had been chosen as an All-Star reserve, making for an NBA-record 22nd consecutive appearance on the squad. The possibility of this being James' final game at the Garden sent prices soaring, with even the cheap seats going for $500.

Feb. 1, 2025: 33 points, 12 assists, 11 rebounds, 54% shooting

Game result: 128-112, Lakers win

James truly put on a show against the Knicks in 2025 with a memorable 30-point triple-double. He became the first visiting player with multiple 30-point triple-doubles at Madison Square Garden, including the playoffs. It was also James' 12th career 30-point game as a visiting player at MSG, breaking a tie with Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for second all time.

There was no shortage of big plays from the then-40-year-old star that night, including a thunderous two-handed slam in the fourth quarter that left comedian Chris Rock stunned courtside.

Although James' performance made headlines, it was overshadowed after the game when news broke of the shocking trade that sent Luka Doncic to the Lakers.

Jan. 31, 2023: 28 points, 11 assists, 10 rebounds, 1 steal, 44% shooting

Game result: 129-123, Lakers win

Year 20 or not, James would never miss an opportunity to wow the New York crowd.

It was his first game there since January 2020, and James made it worth the wait. He had his first triple-double of the season as the Lakers squeaked out an overtime victory.

There was buzz heading into the game, with James weeks away from breaking the career scoring record. However, after the game, James focused on his all-around skills instead.

"I just play the game the right way. I approach the game every night only trying to be a triple threat by scoring, rebounding, assisting, defending, and may the chips fall where they may," he said.

Nov. 13, 2017: 23 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks, 50% shooting
Game result: 104-101, Cavaliers win

Though the numbers aren't among James' best at the Garden, it was the on-court antics that became the story when James and Enes Kanter Freedom clashed in the first quarter.

James dunked the ball, and then wouldn't move out of then-Knicks guard Frank Ntilikina's way as he tried to inbound the ball. Kanter Freedom took offense to that, standing up for Ntilikina as James shoved Kanter Freedom, leading to a double technical.

Kanter Freedom said postgame: "I don't care ... what you call yourself. King, Queen, Princess, whatever you are. You know what, we're going to fight and nobody out there [is] going to punk us."

James led a fourth-quarter comeback to win the game and had a response on Instagram.

Dec. 17, 2010: 32 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists, 1 steal, 60.9% shooting
Game result: 113-91, Heat win

In his first game in New York as a member of the Heat, James recorded a highly efficient triple-double. Fans booed him since he didn't join the Knicks in the offseason, but it didn't hinder his play on the court.

The 60.9% shooting from the field marks his third-highest field goal percentage at Madison Square Garden (70% once, 70.6% twice).

Feb. 4, 2009: 52 points, 11 assists, 9 rebounds, 2 blocks, 51.5% shooting
Game result: 107-102, Cavaliers win

James put on a show in arguably the most iconic game he has played at Madison Square Garden. He accounted for nearly half of the Cavaliers' points. His 52 points were his season high at the time.

The performance came two nights after Kobe Bryant set a then-MSG record with 61 points. James became one of two players -- Michael Jordan was the other -- to have multiple 50-point games as a visitor at the present Madison Square Garden.

March 5, 2008: 50 points, 10 assists, 8 rebounds, 4 steals, 53% shooting
Game result: 119-105, Cavaliers win

After dropping 45 points at home against the Knicks in November, James did himself one better at the Garden in March.

He became the first player with at least 50 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds in a game since Kareem Abdul-Jabbar on Jan. 19, 1975, according to The Associated Press. James exited the game to chants of "MVP!" and called the standing ovation "a dream come true."

ESPN Research contributed to this story.

Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City are keeping an eye on the situation of Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold, while Barcelona and Bayern Munich are scouting Aston Villa attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold is considering his future at the Bernabéu, with Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City monitoring his situation, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old is frustrated with limited playing time under José Mourinho, having made just three LaLiga starts this season amid competition from Denzel Dumfries, while his former club Liverpool are looking for reinforcements at right back following Jeremie Frimpong's injury. Meanwhile, Madrid are closing in on an official announcement for a new one-year contract extension with 34-year-old goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, reports Fabrizio Romano.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli is on the brink of F1 history -- but first, there's a car to wash and pranks to pull
stories.summary: On the brink of becoming F1's youngest world champion, Kimi Antonelli reveals how car washes, pub trips and pranks help him cope with fame and pressure.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli likes to make sure his car is clean.

Even before a trip that is likely to end with him becoming Formula 1's youngest world champion, he cannot bring himself to leave before he's completed a familiar ritual: a visit to the car wash in his road car, a Mercedes GT63. The Italian washes it by hand, meticulously, inside and out. Only then can he travel to his next Formula 1 race.

Asked whether or not he times himself at the car wash, 20-year-old Antonelli laughed.

"No, no, no," he replied in a small group interview including ESPN.

"I take my time because it needs to be done well. It needs to be cleaned well. It needs to be dried well, because if you don't dry it well and there's still some water [on it], then, you know, it's weird. It looks dirty. So it needs to be done well and then also inside.

"I take my time. For that, I take my time."

- How Antonelli can win F1 title at U.S. Grand Prix

- Horner: Hamilton keen on Red Bull before Merc move

It's funny, because almost nothing about Antonelli's journey to this point has been an exercise in taking one's time.

The U.S. Grand Prix on Oct. 26 will be the first time in his career he can win the Formula 1 world drivers' championship, even if there's only a slim mathematical chance he will get it done at the Circuit of the Americas. But whether he does it there, or in Mexico City a week later, or in Brazil a week after that, or at the triple header currently slated to finish the season, Antonelli's lead is so big that he almost certainly will at some point in the next two months become the sport's youngest-ever world champion, in just his second season racing in Formula 1. Amid all of that, keeping any semblance of normality has been a challenge in itself.

Which brings us back to the car wash.

"Racing is always on my mind. I try not to think too much about, first of all, the situation I'm in, because I feel like if I would think too much about championship and stuff, I would probably get anxious as well. Also I wouldn't have quality time at home, because I would just be worrying about this."

He then elaborated on his new-found ritual.

"I like to clean my car," Antonelli said. "I never do automatic, you know, with the machine. I always like to wash by hand, myself. Because I love cars, I really like to take care of my car and everything. I like to see it clean, so it's an activity I love to do. It's a routine."

Normality and routine has been the name of the game for Antonelli in 2026 as he has tried to fight off the growing realisation of what he's about to achieve. But it has been difficult. He's become a superstar in Italy, almost overnight, with his legendary status at home cemented in September with his astonishing victory from 19th on the grid at the Italian Grand Prix. It made him the first Italian winner of that race since 1966 and will go down as the crowning moment of a season which will end with him becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. A nation so regularly tortured by Ferrari's disappointments over the past two decades has had a singular new star to rally around.

That would be a lot for anyone to shoulder -- let alone someone who had only turned 20 two weeks before he stood on the top step of Monza's iconic podium stage.

Asked how he has processed becoming Italy's biggest sporting icon so young, he shrugged, and shook his head, almost as if still unable to fully comprehend it all.

"I try to realise the least as possible," he said. "The situation I'm in, and also the person I'm becoming ... whenever I go back home, I want to feel as normal as possible."

Key to that has been Antonelli's school friends -- the same he studied with last year, when his mother insisted that he had to finish his exams even if he had become a Formula 1 rookie at 18. The same friends who came to support him in the paddock at the Imola race, a stone's throw away from hometown Bologna, last year.

"The situation I'm in and also the person I'm becoming ... whenever I go back home, I want to feel as normal as possible," he said. "I always try to do the normal things, like every human being. So, go to the supermarket, go, to the cinema ... it's more difficult, but I still do so.

"I go with my friends to the pub to watch sport. Especially when we have a weekend off and there's racing, or there's tennis, or any kind of sport. I like to go to the pub with my friends and watch from there, or play bowling, this kind of stuff.

"Whenever I go back home, I try to live a normal life. Of course, it's not easy at times, because whenever you go, it's harder to get the same amount of privacy."

Antonelli's claims of trips to the car wash, the pub, the supermarket and bowling alley would be harder to fathom if he lived in the big city or in a bustling modern town, given the harsh combination of his enormous fame and the social media age he's grown into. While most of his F1 rivals live in Monaco, he now resides in San Marino, the small republic housed inside Italy, about 80 miles from Bologna.

"I like San Marino because it's very small and basically everyone knows each other. You don't get asked for pictures anymore because it's always the same people. I think it's really cool.

"But yeah, whenever I go back home, I just try to live a normal life, not think too much about racing and just enjoy the time with my friends, family, because it also helps me to disconnect a little bit and especially get out from this external bubble that we are in, especially when we're at the race weekend."

From raw rookie to F1 superstar
It seemed to be an enormous gamble, to put it mildly, when Mercedes boss Toto Wolff decided that the man to replace the Ferrari-bound Lewis Hamilton, F1's most accomplished driver, in 2025 should in fact be a teenager. Antonelli, the exciting, but untested prodigy on Mercedes' junior programme, was given the nod.

The narrative that it was too much too soon was easy to write -- Antonelli crashed out of his first practice run at Monza in August 2024, a day before the team made the official confirmation. Wolff later admitted the free practice appearance in front of a frenzied Italian media and fanbase had been ill-advised. After that crash, Mercedes' boss gave his viewpoint on Antonelli's raw, then-unpolished talent, one he has repeated in some form or another a lot over the next two years: "It's always easier to calm down a fast horse than to make a slow horse fast."

Wolff and Mercedes had to echo that viewpoint a lot in 2025. Antonelli's rookie season was a rollercoaster -- especially in a dismal run of European races in the middle of the year, which included a collision with Max Verstappen in Austria and Charles Leclerc in the Netherlands -- and the stark contrast to teammate George Russell's superb and consistent performances in the other car made it easy to anoint the British driver as preseason favourite coming into a new season and rules set which re-established Mercedes as the benchmark team to beat. But Antonelli went into the winter break with a chance to take stock at the opportunity he had been given.

"It was mainly digesting. The first season, you're naturally a bit more tense," he said.

"I felt like I mainly needed time, to digest, to look at the season again. Understand what was good about the season, what was not good. And understanding as well, what was good for me."

Antonelli, who has admitted he tried to do too much as a rookie, both on and off track, came into the new season a changed man. After Russell won the opening race in Australia, Antonelli claimed an emotional maiden win in China and then won the next four in a row in Japan, Miami, Canada and Monaco. He's not looked back since. He snuffed out a brief Russell fightback by winning in Belgium in July, before the Italy win was followed up by victory at Madring's first Spanish Grand Prix.

Even to Antonelli, the contrast between life as an overthinking rookie and a championship leader is night and day.

"It's pretty insane, the step," he admitted. "Because, for sure, having a fast car helps. Obviously. [But] I wouldn't have expected to be a contender like this, this season. Of course, I find myself in this position and I'm very happy, very grateful to be in this position and I've got to keep pushing.

"But ... definitely, at the start of the year, I would have never thought to be in this position. Especially because we were confident with the car, I knew I could have fought for wins. A few wins, podiums. But to be in this position? For sure not. But it was a very nice surprise.

"And now we've just got to finish the job."

He pointed to the Monza victory as the best example of how he's changed things.

"Last year, at the home race, the way it was managed was not good. The way I managed myself. While this year, I feel like, on things that are less important, I leant a lot on the people that I have around [me]. So they take care of it and I don't have to worry about [those things].

"The only thing I worry about is going on track and doing the best I can. While last year, I was worrying about way too many things. Especially my home race. And that's why I felt so drained, mentally, so early into the weekend.

"While this year, I feel in a much better place. Much more protected. Also because the things that I tried to take care of last year, this year the team was taking care of, the people working with me. I could focus on the important things. That has been a big thing for me."

The prankster world champion
Those close to Antonelli will all tell you the same thing: becoming F1's newest superstar has not changed him at all. Antonelli's happy-go-lucky approach to life seemed perfect for a teenage rookie -- but many at Mercedes wondered how long that would last through his elevation to a championship contender.

But rather than becoming a pressure-cooker environment, things have flipped around, something he said he notices in how he interacts with race engineer Peter Bonnington, who works with Antonelli now having guided Hamilton to his six championships at Mercedes.

"This is more relaxed," he said. "You have more confidence with the team. You know each other better. Last year, for example, with Bono.

"As an Italian, I like to give hugs. For example, after a race, after a great result, I like to go there and give him a hug. Share the moment. And last year, it would get very tense at times. You could see it would tense up. But this year, he actually enjoys it. Because he knows it's part of myself as well.

"But also, he enjoys it. He probably won't admit it, but he does. He does enjoy it."

Bonnington has been on the receiving end of a lot of Antonelli's mischief this year -- the team's Instagram account has recorded several pranks at the race engineer's expense, including Antonelli putting chilli sauce in his drink during preseason testing, and having his key card for Mercedes' F1 headquarters turned off during a visit ahead of the summer break.

Antonelli's boyish enthusiasm for japes has extended to the whole team. After the summer break, a fake interview was set up by the team in the paddock, giving 19 mechanics an opportunity to ambush the Italian and cover him in plates of cream.

During our interview, Antonelli started laughing and briefly asked to go off record so he could detail his next devious plan.

He then ran through a list of people who have been on the receiving end through the season, but there was one obvious name missing.

Asked if he has ever dared prank Wolff, Antonelli laughed.

The young man on the verge of achieving the biggest thing in all of motor racing admitted he still needs to work up the courage for that.

"This is next level," he said in reply. "You need to have big balls to do that!"

Of course, Antonelli might just have the confidence needed to do it by the end of the year.

"I'm going to have to finish well in the championship, finish well this year. Then I have a reason to do it [to Wolff].

"And so then he won't complain too much about it! But that's like next level."

stories.headline: Which MLB teams have never won a World Series?
stories.summary: Five MLB franchises have yet to hoist the Commissioner's Trophy. Let's examine each team and how close they've come to winning a World Series.
stories.body:
Twenty-five of MLB's 30 teams have won at least one World Series. Five franchises have yet to hoist the Commissioner's Trophy: the Colorado Rockies, Milwaukee Brewers, San Diego Padres, Seattle Mariners and Tampa Bay Rays.

The list will shrink this year, as the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers face off in the 2026 World Series.

Let's examine each team and how close they've come to winning a title.

Colorado Rockies

Founded in 1993, the Rockies have made just one World Series appearance. In 2007, Colorado was swept by the Boston Red Sox. The Rockies have never won their division, and they've made just five wild-card berths in their franchise history.

Milwaukee Brewers

Founded in 1970, the Brewers have appeared in the World Series just once. In 1982, Milwaukee lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games. In 2018, the Brewers advanced to the NLCS, but they were ultimately eliminated by the Los Angeles Dodgers, 4-3. In 2026, they punched their ticket to another NLCS versus the Dodgers and advanced to the World Series.

San Diego Padres

Founded in 1969, the Padres have played in the World Series twice. In 1984, they lost to the Detroit Tigers in five games. In 1998, San Diego was swept by the New York Yankees. The Padres are MLB's oldest team without a World Series title.

Seattle Mariners

Founded in 1977, the Mariners have never advanced to the World Series. They have six playoff appearances in their franchise's history. In 2025, Seattle punched their fourth ticket to the ALCS versus the Toronto Blue Jays, but failed to clinch a World Series berth in a pivotal Game 7. They previously lost the ALCS series in 1995, 2000, and 2001.

Tampa Bay Rays

Founded in 1998, the Rays have advanced to the World Series three times. In 2008, Tampa Bay lost to the Philadelphia Phillies in five games. In 2020, the Rays were defeated by the Dodgers in six games. In 2026, they play the Milwaukee Brewers for the championship.

stories.body:
Lisandro Martínez and Marcus Rashford missed training ahead of the trip to Como as Manchester United's injury problems continued to mount.

Martínez's eventful week, which saw him apologise after publicly criticising the club's hierarchy, ended with him keeping his place for Sunday's Premier League clash against Leeds only to be forced off with a thigh complaint.

Rashford was an unused substitute at Elland Road and United confirmed on Tuesday that he is "managing an injury issue."

The England forward and Martínez were among eight players who missed training at Carrington along with Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw, Kobbie Mainoo, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte.

Shaw and Mainoo have both missed the last two matches, Heaven was absent from the Leeds game through illness, while Sesko, Dorgu and Ugarte are all injured.

Meanwhile, Matthijs de Ligt is back in training but has not yet featured following back surgery while fellow defender Lenny Yoro is suspended for the Champions League clash in Italy.
